extracted.intended_audience: PR and communications professionals, marketers, startup founders, and small-business teams preparing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting and distributing press releases across common types (product launches, company news, events, data reports), including required components, length, and distribution tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release purpose (informational, not editorial)
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release is 'an official statement or proclamation announcing news that provides relevant information to the media.' It's fundamentally informational rather than editorial—designed to announce newsworthy developments that journalists can build upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid opinionated or promotional editorializing; focus on newsworthy facts journalists can use to craft stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product or brand launch suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use press releases to announce new offerings to reach potential customers through industry publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only warrant press releases when sufficiently novel; minor updates or incremental changes are better communicated via email campaigns. Assess novelty before choosing a press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company news newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Company announcements cover executive hires, partnerships, mergers, awards, and milestones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key test: Does this impact people outside the organization? If not, it may not be suitable for a press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event announcement focus and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Event announcements promote conferences, webinars, or in-person gatherings with the primary goal of driving attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the 5 W's (who, what, when, where, why) throughout the release and make attendance-oriented details clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-driven report criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Release research or data-driven reports that contain proprietary insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists prize data-driven releases because they establish thought leadership and can remain relevant for years. Ensure methodology and proprietary value are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline should be concise, engaging, and benefit-focused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a short headline that highlights the news value or benefit to readers; avoid vague or overly clever headlines that obscure the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly display when the news is being released so journalists and readers know timing and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead-in (branded opening statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a branded opening statement (lead-in) that sets context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the lead to summarize the most newsworthy angle and connect the announcement to the brand quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key facts (8–13 takeaways)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a concise bulletized set of the most important data points or facts journalists are likely to use; aim for 8–13 items to be thorough but readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes: voice and length
rubrics_metrics.description: Include quotes from executives or stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide 2–4 sentence quotes that add perspective or interpretation but avoid long monologues; quotes should humanize or contextualize the facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-to-action (CTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include clear CTAs such as registration links, landing pages, or website URLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it easy for readers and journalists to take the next step (register, download, learn more) by including direct, trackable links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief company background for unfamiliar readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a short boilerplate that succinctly explains who you are and what you do, so journalists can use it without additional research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide PR team details as the media gatekeeper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List a media contact (name, email, phone) so journalists know who to reach for interviews, assets, or follow-up questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media assets inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Include infographics, videos, or data visualizations when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or link to high-quality media assets to increase engagement and make it easier for outlets to run richer stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Target word counts for press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for 600–800 words for standard announcements; data-driven reports may exceed 1,000 words. Keep releases concise while including necessary detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use visuals for engagement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visuals (charts, photos, graphics) increase pickup and readability—use them when they add value to the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading and polish
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use editing tools (e.g., Grammarly) and multiple reviews to eliminate errors; sloppy releases harm credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution strategy and tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribute strategically using platforms for tracking opens and clicks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use distribution services (such as BuzzStream) to monitor engagement metrics and target outreach; strategic distribution improves pickup and follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of templates by release type
rubrics_metrics.description: There are ready-to-use templates for different release types (general, product launch, company announcement, event promotion, data report).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the template that matches your announcement type to ensure inclusion of appropriate sections and tone.
